note: Early Christian writings outside the New Testament canon. Off by default; optional for comparison only.

entities.label: Didache

scholarly.note: An early church-order text; valued for practice history, but not in the NT canon.

entities.traditionalNote: Early teaching associated with the Twelve—useful historically, not New Testament scripture.
entities.bio: A short manual on the Two Ways, baptism, prayer, Eucharist, and itinerant teachers.

entities.label: 1 Clement

scholarly.note: Letter from the Roman church to Corinth; important for early leadership, outside the NT canon.

entities.traditionalNote: Early letter associated with Clement of Rome; not in the New Testament canon.
entities.bio: Appeals for unity and ordered leadership in Corinth after conflict among believers.

entities.label: Gospel of Thomas

scholarly.dateLabel: Often c. AD 100–140 (some sayings argued earlier)
scholarly.note: A sayings gospel without a passion narrative; clearly outside the fourfold NT Gospel canon.

region.audience: Christian readers outside the canonical Gospels

entities.traditionalNote: Not one of the four canonical Gospels; a later sayings collection.
entities.bio: A list of sayings attributed to Jesus, without the narrative structure of Matthew–John.
kings: Trajanic / Hadrianic period for many manuscript traditions

entities.label: Shepherd of Hermas

scholarly.note: Widely read in some early churches; even bound with Scripture in a few manuscripts, but not retained in the NT canon.

entities.traditionalNote: Visions and parables on repentance; valued historically, not New Testament scripture.
entities.bio: An extended visionary work urging repentance and moral renewal in the early church.

entities.label: Gospel of Peter

scholarly.note: Fragmentary passion/resurrection narrative; historically interesting, not canonical.

entities.traditionalNote: Apocryphal passion gospel; not part of the New Testament.
entities.bio: A surviving portion focuses on the crucifixion and empty tomb with distinctive details.

entities.label: Protoevangelium of James

scholarly.note: Infancy narrative expanding Mary’s story; influential in later piety, not canonical.

region.audience: Christian readers curious about Mary and Jesus’ birth

entities.traditionalNote: Apocryphal infancy gospel; not part of the New Testament.
entities.bio: Narrates Mary’s early life and the nativity with details beyond Matthew and Luke.
